headline: Duke researchers have won up to $15.5 million to test an AI agent that would help look after heart failure patients between doctor visits.
score_reason: Concrete funding and plan, but the system is not built or authorized yet.
importance_line: It could bring heart-failure monitoring to patients far from a cardiologist, but safety, cost and FDA authorization are all still unproven.
summary: The Duke Chronicle reports that a Duke team has been awarded up to $15.5 million to help develop and test an AI agent that would support heart failure patients between visits and is meant to be the first such system authorized by the FDA. It is part of a $62.7 million US government health research program called ADVOCATE, with Duke expecting a real-world trial within two years; a researcher says a human stays in the loop and cost remains an open question.
notes: The goal is FDA authorization; none exists yet. Single student-run outlet; award date not stated.
